chapter: Chicago memories and the road to the Navy
title: Chicago gangster hangouts and the New Deal Club
summary: Chicago meant seeing nothing; Zutty played Greenwood Gardens, a hangout of Capone's brother. He retells how Marge filled in at the New Deal Club, with Reuben Reeves, the gangsters' sons and no shooting.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: END OF TAPE 4
That was Chicago, boy. That was really it.
Well I mean Earl says you had to be like the three monkeys.
Yes.
See nothing, hear nothing, say nothing.
Like we used to play at the Greenwood Gardens and that's where Bottle$Capone used to hang out.
What was that name?
Bottles.
Bottles.
That was his brother.
Oh yes?
Yes.
Well what happened there?
Well just a gangster hangout.
Yes I see.

Like that New Deal in Chicago they had a lot of football players and all that hung out there. But they were gangsters really running it. But old Zutty's piano player called up two hours before time to go to work on Sunday that he couldn't make the Deal. Zutty was half afraid to go to work because he had no piano player and they were liable to whip him or something. (LAUGHTER). And I said, well I'll go with you. I'll sit in.
That's when I told you about the long finger nails.

I said I'd go because Zutty said I don't know what I'm going to do because can't get any piano player on a Sunday two hours ahead, just before he had to go to work. And Zutty said, those guys are so rough over there.
Did you see much rough stuff or shooting while you were there?
No I didn't see no shooting.
But they were rough guys.
I don't remember, seeing any shooting.
And boy I took my wrist band Swung 'em into and I bad health. (LAUGHTER). Ruebin Reeves
And was on the trumpet.
Yes, on the trumpet. And I and Zutty looked like he wanted to .......
He was pushing Louis there for a time.
Well Ruebin wasn't bad though was he? Where did Ruebin come from?
I don't know. It was either Sand Katz Chicago because when he played in that 'Battling Cats'
theater there with Dave Peyton, man that cat was too much.
Yes I mean he was, he never got much credit though.
But that was really funny because ......
What a trumpet player. Red Rueben Reeves.
I hadn't played for such a long time and Zutty looked like he was so worried. Half afraid to go to work. He didn't have a piano player. You had three pieces, you had three or four pieces.
You see all the big gangsters sons used to hang out in this....
Small fry.
Football players and everything.
They called them the bone crushers (bruisers). And they sponsored a football team.

And I'm telling you, I said well Zutty, I said, well I'll go with you to halp you out. And Zutty said yes. And I had a wrist band that I wore because my wrist would get so tired. But I could play everything they were going to play. And I swung them into bad health. (LAUGHTER).
Swing them into bad health. How old is that?
I don't know. I've been hearing that a long time.
Yes, and I've been so lucky the things I did.

I guess that must have been old and went out of fashion? But I remember Charlie Carpenter talking about, Charlie Carpenter was talking about Earl somewhere and he says, he swung them into bad health. And that was the first time I had ever heard that.
